faq.a: Aeesha is associated with the Arabic form عائشة, whose core sense is living, alive, prosperous.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aeesha?
faq.a: Aeesha is associated with Arabic. Variant romanization of عائشة (ʿĀʾisha), feminine of ʿāʾish ('living').
Yes — the underlying form عائشة is Arabic.
Aeesha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

Aeesha should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. عائشة is not a Qur'anic form; it is the name of ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr, a wife of the Prophet, in the hadith and sīra tradition

faq.q: What does Aeesha mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aeesha is rendered عائشہ and carries the sense زندہ، جیتی جاگتی.

faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Aeesha.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aeesha?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aeesha, aeesha. Script forms are عائشة, عائشہ, عايشه, आयशा.

faq.q: Is Aeesha a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
